target_customer: Apartment renters (skewing younger, per Zumper CEO); monetized via listing partners and ads
problem: Rental listings on Craigslist and other sites had no good map view. PadMapper showed listings on a full-screen map with live filters.
business_model: free consumer search funded by listings partnerships and advertising

founders.name: Eric DeMenthon
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch 2012 name him as founder and creator; he joined Zumper after the 2016 deal. No sourced prior employers or education found.

founders.name: Rob Crowell
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2016 names him CTO; he joined Zumper. Not listed as co-founder on the YC page, so recorded as CTO only.

exit.reason: CEO of Zumper said the price was under 10 million dollars in cash and stock; the deal closed January 2016 and was announced 25 Feb 2016.

technical_complexity.rationale: A map interface over aggregated listings with real-time filtering. Scraping and map rendering at scale were the hard parts for a team of two.

defensibility.rationale: Dependent on Craigslist data, which Craigslist cut off in 2012, and Craigslist then added its own maps. The interface was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Craigslist sent a cease and desist in June 2012, sued in July 2012 and later settled; it added its own map view in 2012. Zumper bought PadMapper in 2016.

market_need_then: Renters searched on Craigslist, which lacked map browsing. TechCrunch 2012 cites the founder claiming many millions of users depended on PadMapper.

branding.domain_note: padmapper.com is still live and powered by Zumper, per its site in 2026.

identity.logo: Replaced by a new logo introduced when Zumper relaunched the brand in February 2016, designed to convey a trusted and playful feel.
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Making Apartment Hunting Suck Less.

rebrands.why: Refresh at the Zumper relaunch, per Inman and PadMapper blog coverage

branding.community_and_virality: Craigslist's lawsuit gave it wide press and sympathy; Lifehacker and others covered it. Friends call it a mashup of Google Maps and Craigslist per TechCrunch 2012.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that said what it did, strong press, and a brand kept alive as a Zumper subsidiary for years after the sale.

outcome_analysis: PadMapper grew organically from a student project without outside funding to millions of users, but its main data source, Craigslist, sent a cease and desist in June 2012 and sued in July, then added maps itself. It settled and later sold to Zumper in January 2016 for under 10 million dollars in cash and stock. The brand lives on as a Zumper subsidiary. The capital efficient start and sticky name helped it survive a platform dispute.
notes: TechCrunch 2016 states PadMapper never raised outside funding, so rounds is empty and coverage is complete; Dealroom also shows zero. BuzzFeed says it started in 2009 and YC lists Summer 2010. Craigslist platform dependency is sourced from TechCrunch 2012 and search coverage of the lawsuit; settlement terms are not verified (one low-quality source claims a payment to EFF). Competitors dated to 2010 were not found in opened sources, so the list is empty. Education and prior employers of the founders were not found in opened sources.
